short: Trading enterprise established to secure Swedish interests in the West African gold and slave trades.
full:
Founded in 1649, the Swedish Africa Company was chartered to establish trading posts on the Gold Coast in present-day Ghana. The enterprise was part of a broader mercantile strategy to bypass European middlemen and directly access lucrative colonial markets, particularly for gold, ivory, and enslaved people.

The company established several forts, most notably Carolusborg (Cape Coast Castle). However, the venture was chronically underfunded and faced intense competition from the Dutch and Danish West India Companies. By 1663, its remaining assets had been seized or sold, marking an early and unsuccessful end to Sweden's African colonial ambitions.
